title: fix: isolate unhealthy timers by RoleInstanceSet
premise: observeInstanceHealth keys instanceUnhealthySince by RoleInstance UID only and its cleanup deletes any UID absent from the current set's instances; reconciling set B wipes set A's unhealthy start time (and vice versa), so neither set's 10s unhealthy window matures under interleaving and both rollouts stay stuck on the old template. #470's timed retries bring the controller back but cannot help while the start time keeps being deleted.

findings.summary: pruneInstanceHealth ranges the entire global map and does a lister Get per entry on every Reconcile (O(N) per reconcile), even when only this set's entries exist.

pruneInstanceHealth treats informer-cache IsNotFound as definitive and deletes OTHER sets' timers; a transient cache desync (existing set momentarily absent from cache) would wipe another set's timer — the same cross-set reset class the PR fixes, triggered by cache inconsistency rather than the cleanup loop.
